name: socat
one_line: multipurpose relay: connect two data streams
plain: `socat` (SOcket CAT) connects any two 'addresses' and copies data between them: a TCP port and a file, a terminal and a network connection, one port and another port, a Unix socket and a TCP port. It is netcat with many more kinds of endpoint.
The shape is `socat ADDRESS1 ADDRESS2`. Each address is a type plus options, such as `TCP-LISTEN:8080,fork,reuseaddr` or `TCP:10.10.10.5:80`.
Typical uses are port forwarding, relaying between networks, TLS wrapping, serving a program on a port in a lab, and talking to Unix sockets.
when: Forward a local port to a remote host (pivoting in a lab).
Relay or log traffic between two sides.
Wrap a plain service in TLS.
Test a service by hand with line editing.
Talk to a Unix socket such as /var/run/docker.sock.

examples.explain: - is the terminal (stdin/stdout). Type an HTTP request and see the reply.

examples.title: Listen and print
examples.explain: Waits for a connection on 4444 and prints what arrives: a netcat-style listener.

examples.title: Forward a port
examples.explain: Anything sent to your port 8080 goes to 10.10.10.5:80. fork lets several connections work at once.

examples.title: Serve a file
examples.explain: Each connection reads the file. Useful for quick file transfer in a lab.

examples.title: Receive a file
examples.explain: Saves whatever is sent to received.bin.

examples.title: Log both directions
examples.explain: -v prints the traffic as text, so the relay doubles as a simple proxy log.

examples.title: Talk to a Unix socket
examples.explain: Lets you send raw HTTP to the Docker API on its socket.

examples.title: TLS wrapper
examples.explain: Accepts TLS connections and passes them on in plain text to a local service (needs a certificate).

examples.title: A better line editor
examples.explain: READLINE gives you history and editing while talking to a service.

mistakes: Forgetting fork on a listener: it accepts one connection and then exits.
Forgetting reuseaddr and getting 'address already in use' on restart.
Listening on all interfaces when localhost is enough: add bind=127.0.0.1.
Exposing a relay to the internet by accident.
Using EXEC/SYSTEM endpoints on machines you do not control.
